name: 2.5D Task 4 / 4A — board background, bucketed blank bodies, the face atlas, and the decoupled shadow assets
status: Tasks 4 and 4A of 2_5d_implementation_plan.md, on the Task 3 runtime layout. Writes the static 2D assets the Task 5/6 compositor reconstructs the table from: one empty-board render, exactly one perspective blank body per bucket the layout emitted, one flat 37-face atlas (Task 4), plus the per-bucket cast mat shadows, the wall-stack contact decal and the four normalized crevice masks (Task 4A). The blanks carry no external drop shadows: the shadow assets are separate sprites the runtime draws from the live board state, so nothing baked into a body has to be stripped again.

scene.note: The Task 2 rig scene, built by bake_table_reference.build_scene in its --rig mode with the spec's default variant. The blanks keep the resolved camera and the rig lights (including the hand lighting cheat) so a blank is shaded exactly like the reference render's own tile; only one body is visible per render, and the board (mat, rim, centre well, floor) is hidden. The board render keeps the table meshes and hides every tile, decal and shadow helper.

board.note: The empty table at the reference resolution: playing mat, raised rim, recessed centre well and the dark room floor behind them, with every tile, decal and hand-shadow helper hidden. Film is opaque so the board is a complete backdrop; Task 6 draws it first and never needs a page colour behind it. The rig's own reference render is RGBA/transparent and calibration-only; this one is a runtime asset.

blanks.note: One RGBA sprite per bucket in table_layout.json's bucketCatalogue, rendered from the catalogue's representative slot so the perspective is the slot's own. The sprite is rendered at pixelRatio x the 1920 x 1080 contract frame, cropped to the alpha bounds plus paddingPx, and published with a pixel pivot (the representative slot's exported anchor) and the slot's projected faceQuad in sprite pixels. Nothing but the one tile body is visible: film transparent, no floor, no shadow catcher, so alpha contains no cast shadow, only the body's own bevel self-shading.
blanks.opponentHands: The five hand buckets are drawn from hand_south by the Task 3 catalogue, so the blank is the ivory front the player sees. The north/west/east hands stand with their blue backs to the camera and are not covered by a second bucket family: the plan fixes the five names and the under-20-file acceptance, and table-reference-spec.json already records the share as a Task 4 asset decision. Task 5/6 must either add blue-back hand blanks or reuse the wall/blue body; this is recorded here rather than invented as a silent sixth hand bucket.

atlas.order: 34 standard faces (1m-9m, 1p-9p, 1s-9s, 1z-7z) then the three red fives (5mr, 5pr, 5sr, with the task's 0m/0p/0s aliases), row-major. The order and the cell rects are the stable contract Task 4B's carved bake and Task 5's flat compositor both reference; append new faces after the reds, never re-sort the existing 37.
atlas.note: Flat orthographic glyphs on transparent cells, rasterised by the same pinned resvg configuration as faces.json: one 288 x 384 master per face, the upstream symbol-only SVG's uniform 0.96 scale and 300 x 400 canvas margins, red fills recoloured with faces-spec.json's paint pair. No perspective, no body shading, and no per-bucket variants. 6 x 7 cells holds the 37 faces in the same 6-column arrangement as the Task 4B relief atlas; the empty cells stay fully transparent.

matPlane.note: A 30-unit neutral plane at the mat's z (0) is the only geometry besides the one caster: the mat, rim, floor, other tiles and the rig's hand-shadow helpers are hidden, so the recorded darkening is the tile's own. It is a plain diffuse plane, not Blender's shadow-catcher pass, because the bake needs an interpretable alpha it can measure (the ratio of lit to shadowed luma) rather than a special-case render output.

shadows.note: Task 4A: one cast shadow per sprite bucket plus the wall-stack contact decal. alpha = 1 - shadowedLuma/litLuma, published as black ink so source-over reproduces a multiply. A wall bucket's representative is a top-tier tile, so its shadow is measured from the same body dropped onto z = 0 and is drawn at the stack's bottom-tier anchor; layer 1 never draws a mat shadow (its occlusion of the tile under it is the stack decal). noiseFloor is 5/255: below 2 % the ratio is the two renders' residual difference (bounce light and the denoiser), not shadow, and a 2 % multiplier is invisible on the felt. --bake needs Blender 4.5.9; --check does not.

crevices.note: The four inter-tile bevel-crevice masks, authored in normalized face UV (0..1 square) so one mask maps onto any bucket's faceQuad. Grayscale black ink with the AO in alpha, written by scripts/bake-shadow-seams.mjs with no Blender. The profile is a raised cosine from peakAlpha at the outer bevel edge to 0 at the fade width: no hard cut, no banding. The fade is set per axis so the physical band is the bevel's own width on all four edges (0.10 of the 21 mm width along u, 0.075 of the 28 mm height along v = the same 0.10 of tile width).

checks.note: Task 4A's acceptance in numbers: every mat shadow has a real darkening core, a support area big enough to be a cast shadow and a penumbra outside the body footprint on at least two sides; the wall decal has a contact core; each seam mask peaks at about 35% black on the outer edge, falls monotonically to zero within 8-12% of the tile width, and is constant along its own edge.

Thresholds are the plan's Task 4 acceptance in numbers, not a look: under 20 blank files, every blank has an opaque body, an anti-aliased edge and a fully transparent padding border, no alpha more than noHaloPx outside the body (a cast shadow would be), the board is opaque at its full resolution, and the atlas holds 37 non-overlapping inked cells (haku is a real face with zero ink, recorded like faces.json does).
